request: Persist banner data and artwork so a full relaunch does not wait for network.
causes: Public banner list was cached only in process memory.
Public catalog query was followed by a blocking presentation callable, then image downloads.
One live artwork response required HTTP revalidation (private,max-age=0).

liveReadOnlyBaseline.context: Read-only Mac network probe; not physical iPhone startup trace

fixes: Live AppContainer uses an on-disk public catalog cache. Mock graphs remain memory-only.
Restoration publishes usable cached content before awaiting network; restored catalogs always revalidate. Authoritative empty response replaces cached content and persists the removal.
Cache lifetime capped at24hours; begin/end/countdown-hide deadlines and region/placement filters apply before display. Corrupt, oversized, future-dated and unsupported-version cache data is ignored.
Owner edits invalidate the persisted catalog as well as memory. Queued atomic disk writes run off main, with restoration generation protection.

Banner artwork has a revision-keyed disk cache:20MiB/32file budget,8MiB maximum object,24hour age cap. New banner revision cannot reuse old artwork even at the same URL. A disk miss fetches fresh bytes; successfully decoded images only are persisted.
Common remote-image HTTP policy is retained for non-banner images; banner cache is opt-in. Image decoding remains off main.
Cold first-ever launch still needs network. Warmed data/artwork survive process termination; no extra server charges for keeping warm function instances and no server/rules/schema changes.

fullUnits.boundary: Opt-in SDK tests skipped, not counted as passed. This change has no server mutations.

coldProcessRelaunch.coverage: Seed catalog and real JPEG into isolated disk caches, terminate app, relaunch fresh process. Actual RemoteImageView displays artwork before a deliberately suspended repository replies, with image URL pointing at unreachable127.0.0.1:1. Then empty server result removes banner.

freshnessBoundary: Offline cached banners can reflect their last verified remote active state until the24hour cap; unknown remote deletions/deactivations cannot be detected without connectivity. Known schedule deadlines are enforced locally. Successful empty remote result removes cached items immediately.
